name: Back-rank mate
definition: Mate delivered on the king's home rank when the king is walled in by its own pawns with no luft.

name: Smothered mate
definition: Knight mate against a king fully surrounded by its own pieces, usually after a queen sacrifice that forces self-block.

name: Anastasia's mate
definition: Mating net with a knight cutting off flight squares and a rook/queen delivering mate along the file or rank.

name: Arabian mate
definition: Rook + knight mate against a king in the corner; rook on the edge, knight covering the escape.

name: Boden's mate
definition: Two bishops on criss-crossing diagonals mate a castled king, usually after a queen sacrifice that opens lines.

name: Damiano's mate
definition: Queen + pawn mate on h7/h2 after sacrifices that force the king to the corner and clear the h-file.

name: Kingside attack mate
definition: Mate arising from a direct attack on the castled king using multiple attackers on the g/h files or 6th/7th rank.

name: Knight fork
definition: A single knight attacks two or more enemy pieces simultaneously; the defender cannot save both.

name: Pawn fork
definition: A pawn advance attacks two enemy pieces at once, winning material since at most one can retreat.

name: Queen fork
definition: Queen attacks two enemy pieces simultaneously, often including the king, forcing material loss.

name: Royal fork
definition: Fork of king and queen (or other royal piece) — typically by a knight — winning the queen after the forced king move.

name: Double attack
definition: A single move creates two distinct threats (not necessarily a fork by one piece); the opponent cannot parry both.

name: Absolute pin
definition: A piece is pinned against its own king — it cannot legally move off the attacking line.

name: Relative pin
definition: A piece is pinned against a more valuable piece behind it; moving it is legal but loses material.

name: Skewer
definition: Attack on a high-value piece that, when it moves, exposes a lower-value piece behind it on the same line.

name: Discovered attack
definition: Moving one piece uncovers an attack from another piece behind it along the line.

name: Discovered check
definition: Discovered attack where the unmasked piece delivers check — the moving piece is free to make additional threats.

name: Double check
definition: Two pieces check the king simultaneously via discovered check; the king must move — blocking and capturing are both impossible.

name: X-ray attack
definition: An attack 'through' an enemy piece — the attacker eyes a target that lies behind the blocker on the same line.

name: Windmill
definition: Repeating pattern of discovered check and direct check that picks off enemy pieces each cycle.

name: Zwischenzug (in-between move)
definition: An unexpected move that interrupts an expected sequence, imposing a threat that must be addressed first.

name: Desperado
definition: A doomed piece sells itself as dearly as possible by capturing or trading before it is lost.

name: Deflection
definition: A piece defending a key square or piece is forced to abandon its duty by a threat elsewhere.

name: Decoy
definition: Forcing an enemy piece onto a bad square where it can be attacked, pinned, or used to block its own forces.

name: Attraction
definition: Sacrifice that lures the enemy king or piece to a square where it falls to a follow-up tactic.

name: Interference
definition: Placing a piece between two enemy pieces that defend each other, breaking the defensive link.

name: Clearance sacrifice
definition: Sacrificing a piece to vacate a square, file, or diagonal that is needed by another attacker.

name: Overloaded piece
definition: A defender is tasked with too many duties; attacking one forces it to abandon another.

name: Removing the defender
definition: Capturing or forcing away the sole defender of a target piece or key square.

name: Trapped piece
definition: A piece with no safe retreat squares, often caught by a pawn advance or coordinated pieces.

name: Underpromotion tactic
definition: Promoting to a knight, bishop, or rook — not queen — to deliver check, fork, or avoid stalemate.

name: Quiet move
definition: A non-capturing, non-checking move that sets up an unavoidable threat — the hardest class of tactic to see.

name: Counterattack
definition: Meeting a threat not by defending but by creating a larger counter-threat elsewhere.

name: IQP — attacker's play
definition: Using the space, outpost on e5/d5/e4/d4, and piece activity that the IQP grants the side with it.

name: IQP — defender's play
definition: Blockading the IQP, trading pieces to reach a favorable endgame where the weak pawn becomes the main factor.

name: Minority attack
definition: Advancing the fewer queenside pawns (usually b-pawn) to create a weakness in the opponent's majority.

name: Hanging pawns
definition: Two adjacent pawns (typically c+d) with no neighbors — dynamic when advancing, weak when fixed.

name: Backward pawn exploitation
definition: Piling up on a pawn that cannot advance and is blocked from being defended by its neighbors.

name: Outpost knight
definition: Installing a knight on a strong square in enemy territory that cannot be challenged by a pawn.

name: Bishop pair conversion
definition: Opening the position and coordinating two bishops against a minor-piece pair to convert the long-term advantage.

name: Opposite-side castling attack
definition: Racing pawn storms toward opposite-castled kings — tempo and open files matter more than material.

name: Same-side castling attack
definition: Breaking through a castled king's shelter when kings are on the same wing — piece play, sacrifices, exchange of defenders.

name: King hunt
definition: Chasing an exposed king across the board with successive checks, converting exposure into mate or material.

name: Fortress
definition: Drawing resource where the material-down side erects an impenetrable piece-and-pawn structure.

name: Zugzwang
definition: Any move worsens the position — the obligation to move is itself the losing factor.

name: Prophylaxis
definition: Preventing the opponent's plan before pursuing your own — restricts their options before activity.

name: Weak color complex
definition: Exploiting squares of one color left undefended by a missing bishop or pawn chain.

name: Space advantage
definition: Controlling more squares via advanced pawns; convert by trading the right pieces and opening lines at the right time.

name: Pawn-break timing
definition: Choosing the moment to strike with a thematic pawn break (c4, d5, f4, e5, etc.) to release tension in your favor.

name: Bad bishop vs good knight
definition: Exploiting a bishop hemmed in by its own pawn structure while your knight has strong squares.

name: Exchange sacrifice
definition: Giving up a rook for a minor piece to gain long-term positional compensation — squares, pawn weaknesses, initiative.

name: Positional sacrifice
definition: Sacrificing material for long-term non-forcing compensation (structure, initiative, king safety).

name: Rook lift
definition: Bringing a rook to the 3rd/4th rank via the first rank to support an attack on the king or a thematic advance.

name: Open-file domination
definition: Taking and holding the only open file with rooks, then infiltrating to the 7th/8th rank.

name: Seventh-rank rook
definition: Posting a rook on the 7th rank to attack pawns and restrict the enemy king — 'pigs on the 7th.'

name: Lucena position
definition: Winning technique in R+P vs R when the defender's king is cut off — build a bridge with the rook.

name: Philidor position
definition: Drawing technique in R+P vs R — keep the rook on the 3rd/6th rank, then switch to rear checks.

name: Opposition
definition: Kings face each other with one square between; side-not-to-move has the opposition and controls key squares.

name: Distant opposition
definition: Opposition across multiple empty squares on the same file/rank — converts to direct opposition with correct tempo moves.

name: Triangulation
definition: Maneuvering the king in a triangle to lose a tempo and hand zugzwang to the opponent.

name: Vancura defense
definition: Drawing R vs R+a(or h)-pawn with the rook giving side-checks from the long side — prevents the pawn from advancing.

name: Wrong-colored bishop draw
definition: K+B+rook-pawn where the bishop does not control the promotion square — draw with the defending king in the corner.

name: K+P vs K (square rule)
definition: When the defending king is outside the imaginary square of the passed pawn, the pawn queens without king support.

name: R vs R+P endgame
definition: The fundamental class of rook endings — Philidor, Lucena, Vancura, short-side defense, building a bridge.

name: Two bishops vs bishop + knight
definition: Converting the bishop-pair advantage in open endings by creating a second weakness and dominating the knight.

name: Bishop and knight mate
definition: Forced mate with K+B+N vs K — drive the king to the corner of the bishop's color using the W-maneuver.

name: Q vs P endgame
definition: Winning Q vs advanced pawn by forcing the enemy king in front of its own pawn with repeated checks.

name: Active king in rook endgames
definition: The king as an attacking piece once queens are off — the single biggest factor in rook endgames.

name: Passed-pawn creation
definition: Forcing a passed pawn via pawn breakthroughs, exchanges, or outside-majority play.

name: Pawn breakthrough
definition: Sacrificing pawns to promote one — typically 3-vs-3 pawn-race problems.
